passage: When a gazelle spots a cheetah, it sometimes leaps straight up on stiff legs instead of running away at once. The display burns energy and gives up a head start, so only a gazelle fit enough to escape anyway can afford to perform it. Cheetahs, for their part, often abandon a chase after seeing the leap. The display persuades the predator precisely because it is ______: a weak or injured gazelle could not fake it.
prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explanation: The text says the leap burns energy and gives up a head start, so only a fit gazelle can afford it; that expense is why a weak animal cannot fake it, making the display "costly." A "clear" display is merely easy to see, an "abrupt" one merely sudden, and a "brief" one merely short, and a weak gazelle could produce a signal with any of those qualities, so none explains why the cheetah is persuaded.
